meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hall, large room; courtroom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лишком').

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'butter, oil' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Add a piece of butter to the pan.

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

examples.text: Добавляем немного сливочного масла и соли.
examples.trans: We add a little butter and salt.

передать.gloss: to pass on, to hand over

meanings.en: to pass on, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pass on, to hand over', paired with 'передавать'.

examples.trans: Please pass on my regards to your mum.

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
Common masculine noun meaning 'cook, chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to redo, to remake', paired with 'переделывать'.

examples.trans: All of this needs to be redone.

examples.text: Я рада. Только всё это нужно переделать.
examples.trans: I'm glad. Only all of this needs to be redone.
Only all of this needs to be redone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'алат'). Common masculine noun meaning 'salad' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Седьмой столик заказал салат с трюфелями.
examples.trans: Table seven ordered a salad with truffles.

examples.text: Гость пришёл специально ради этого салата.
examples.trans: The guest came especially for this salad.

просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Samsonov, I asked you not to!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to charge ahead, push forward', paired with 'попереть'.

examples.trans: Your Samsonov is charging ahead like a tank!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'изойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to happen', paired with 'происходить'.

examples.text: Я не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know how it happened.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to happen, go on', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?
